Energy transition

Paradise

Honolulu has plenty of sun and wind. On a calm night, you're paying for imported oil. There's no neighboring grid to buy power from.

Play Paradise↗ Your decisions ↓

Choose your difficulty before you start. It’s free to play in your browser.

Location
Honolulu, Hawaii
Starts in
2003
Your term
13 years

Your starting point

Take over an island utility in 2003. Its wind and solar farms already supply some electricity, but much of its capacity comes from an oil plant.

A delayed fuel shipment will push up oil prices. Every unit of electricity you can generate locally without oil is one less you have to pay that higher price for.

Learn how to play

Your decisions

  1. 01

    Decide what to build on the island

    Compare the cost of a wind or solar project with the oil purchases it could save over its lifetime.

  2. 02

    Save power for the evening

    Look for hours when your wind and solar farms have electricity to spare. How much could you store for later?

  3. 03

    Allow for visitors

    Electricity use rises during the visitor boom. Check whether enough local supply will be ready for the extra demand.

What would it take to burn less oil after sunset?
